title: HD 139139 dip durations reject an equal-speed random-chord model under Gaussian errors and monotone selection
abstract: We test the 28 published HD 139139 dip durations against small objects with one projected speed and independent uniform impact parameters. A scale-free count bound allows unknown speed and any detection probability that does not fall with duration. Gaussian marginal duration errors and three exploratory thresholds give a conservative tail bound of 0.00389. If one event can be arbitrary, the bound rises to 0.146. Thus the result constrains the narrow model but is not robust to an arbitrary single bad event. It confirms no new dip, object or physical cause. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure and exact external-source retrieval steps are included. The source table stays outside the baseline package.
